title: 叠加定理：电流可以叠加，功率不能
statement: 图示电路中 V_s1 = 12 V，V_s2 = 6 V，R_1 = R_2 = 2 Ω，R_3 = 1 Ω。
用叠加定理求 R_3 中的电流 i_3，并求 R_3 吸收的功率 P_3。再思考：能否把两个电源各自单独作用时 R_3 的功率相加得到 P_3？

questions.explain: 必须先叠加电流再算功率：P_3 = i_3²·R_3 = 4.5² × 1 = 20.25 W。

questions.ask: V_s1、V_s2 单独作用时 R_3 的功率分别是 9 W 和 2.25 W，和为 11.25 W，与 P_3 不等。原因是：
choices: 功率是电流（电压）的二次函数，不是线性量，所以不满足叠加
单独作用时电源置零的方法错了
choiceExplain: 与极性无关：即使两个电源极性相同，P = R(i' + i'')² 中的交叉项 2Ri'i'' 仍然存在，只有 i'·i'' = 0 时功率才恰好可加。
置零方法没错（电压源短路）：i_3' + i_3'' = 4.5 A 与直接求解一致，说明各分量本身没有算错。
questions.explain: P = R(i' + i'')² = Ri'² + Ri''² + 2Ri'i''，交叉项 2Ri'i'' = 2 × 3 × 1.5 = 9 W 正好是相差的部分。叠加定理只适用于线性电路中的电压和电流。

hints: 每个电源单独作用时，另一个电压源短路，R_3 与另一侧的 2 Ω 电阻并联。
先叠加电流 i_3 = i_3' + i_3''，再用 P = i²R 求功率。

en.title: Superposition: currents add, powers don't
statement: In the circuit, V_s1 = 12 V, V_s2 = 6 V, R_1 = R_2 = 2 Ω, R_3 = 1 Ω.
Use superposition to find the current i_3 in R_3 and the power P_3 absorbed by R_3. Then think: can you get P_3 by adding the powers in R_3 when each source acts alone?

questions.explain: Superpose the current first, then compute power: P_3 = i_3²·R_3 = 4.5² × 1 = 20.25 W.

questions.ask: With V_s1 or V_s2 acting alone, R_3 absorbs 9 W and 2.25 W; the sum 11.25 W is not P_3. Why?
choices: Power is a quadratic function of current (voltage), not a linear quantity, so it doesn't superpose
The two sources have different polarities
The sources were zeroed the wrong way
choiceExplain: Polarity has nothing to do with it: even with both sources aiding, P = R(i' + i'')² contains the cross term 2Ri'i''; powers add only when i'·i'' = 0.
The sources were zeroed correctly (voltage sources shorted): i_3' + i_3'' = 4.5 A matches the direct solution, so the components themselves are right.
questions.explain: P = R(i' + i'')² = Ri'² + Ri''² + 2Ri'i''; the cross term 2Ri'i'' = 2 × 3 × 1.5 = 9 W is exactly the difference. Superposition applies only to voltages and currents of linear circuits.

hints: With one source acting alone, the other voltage source is a short, so R_3 is in parallel with the 2 Ω resistor on the other side.
Superpose the current first, i_3 = i_3' + i_3'', then use P = i²R.
solution: **4. Power doesn't superpose:** P_3' + P_3'' = 9 + 2.25 = 11.25 W ≠ 20.25 W; the difference is the cross term 2R_3·i_3'·i_3'' = 9 W.
